messages.subject: Porting an existing package to devtools.
messages.subject_clean: Porting an existing package to devtools.
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I have become the maintainer of a package we use at work.

As part of the refactoring I would like to make, the first thing is to have the package working with the devtools workflow.

While I have created and maintained successfully (tiny) R packages starting from scratch I have no experience in "porting"
an existing package to devtools.

I have two tasks I don't know how to tackle though:

1. can I automatically integrate the existing documentation in the R files making them become roxygen comments? (I remember I read something about this a few time ago, but I can't find the link now).
2. this R package depends on other internally hosted packages; is there any way in "Imports" I can specify also the address to the git repository so that dependencies are installed as if they were Cran packages?

Thanks a lot in advance for your help!

Cheers,
Luca

messages.body_plain:
Dear Luca,

On 17 Feb 2015, at 06:41, Gábor Csárdi <csardi...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > 2. this R package depends on other internally hosted packages; is there any
> > > way in "Imports" I can specify also the address to the git repository so
> > > that dependencies are installed as if they were Cran packages?
> >
> > Not currently.
>
> You can try just to copy the R file(s) of these packages into your package. This might work for simple packages without compiled sources, and too many dependencies. It is a pretty bad solution for many reasons, but the only one IMO. (Except for submitting your dependencies to CRAN as well, either by the original author(s), or by you.)

As Hadley and Gabor have pointed out, this is not currently possible. This would of course be very nice and has been discussed on and off e.g. here

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rdevtools/0lpGUyg6470

Jeroen Ooms who started that discussion has written up his opinions on these and related issues in detail here:

http://journal.r-project.org/archive/2013-1/ooms.pdf

Coming back to your problem, you might also be interested in packrat

http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/

This does not solve exactly your problem (although it could certainly help), but you the approach described in this link could be a way forward:

http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/custom-repos.html

Best wishes,

Greg.

I think the RStudio integration of packrat is quite good, but others would have to comment on that as I haven’t really used it seriously.

> I'd like to make the process of installing the package as easy as possible for the others (but I am definitively interested for my personal knowledge)

However, if this is your goal, then either

1. making your own local CRAN repository (as described in the last link,  http://rstudio.github.io/packrat/custom-repos.html but note that providing binary packages for different platforms can be burdensome)

or

2. If code can be made openly available (I’m guessing not) using a) http://rforge.net/ + github or b) http://r-forge.r-project.org/ including svn hosting

could work. In this approach, users need to add an additional repository to their default repository setting but this should not be too complicated to explain.

Best,

Greg.

messages.subject: install_git issues on Windows
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I posted an issue on Github https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/725 .

On my Windows machine I set up ssh, git, R, Rtools, RStudio and I installed devtools.

devtools works fine (what I tried at list), except for the install_url, install_git and so on
hang while Downloading the git repo.

Could you have a look at the issue in Github and help me understand if it is a bug (and if so how to detect it),
or if there is some errors in my configuration?

Thanks a lot in advance for the help,

Cheers,

messages.subject: Utility function to set package options
messages.subject_clean: Utility function to set package options
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody, when writing my functions I always find myself using
a function "pkgoptions" I wrote, which I find quite handy to set and retrieve options package.

When I need some way to set and retrieve options in my package I do the following:

mypkgopt <- pkgoptions()

After that in my code I can set options using mypkgopt("option_name", option_value).

I retrieve the options I have set using mypkgopt("optionname")

And if I want to see all the values I use mypkgopt()

I have tried to check whether a similar function was already implemented in devtools,
but I couldn't find it.

I think due to its generality and utility this function would fit well in devtools (if it is not redundant, if not I would rather learn the "devtools" way).

Since I use devtools mostly as a user I don't have a fork of the repository so I am attacching the file here,
but of course if you think it is useful enough to include it and  prefer that I submit a branch request I can do that.

If you think it is a bad approach I am willing to learn why :)

Cheers,
Luca
